- [Substack: The AI Boom Rolls On: AI Partnerships Pay Off as Stocks Soar & Meta, Google & Microsoft Go All-In](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-ai-boom-rolls-on-ai-partnerships-387) - 2025-10-31

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

The October 31 wrap reviews hyperscaler results and compares their ability to finance AI investment. Eisman also separates resilient card-network spending from Fiserv weakness, persistent housing problems and managed-care strain.

The near-term Nvidia earnings expectation was supported by the following report. The more ambitious Meta-versus-cloud-provider return comparison is not established by market capitalization or cash-balance changes alone. His company differentiation is stronger than blanket claims that rate cuts or AI announcements always help stocks.

<a id="youtube-Lt0xLJJ6sfA-c005"></a>
### 005. Higher hyperscaler spending means Nvidia should report very strong results at its next release.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 4:45-5:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lt0xLJJ6sfA&t=285s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: Next Nvidia quarterly release in November 2025

The November 19 release showed 62% revenue growth, 22% sequential growth and $1.30 EPS. This is a short-horizon operating forecast, not a stock-return guarantee.

Assessment test: Compare the next reported operations with the dated expectation.

- [Nvidia fiscal Q3 2026 results](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-third-quarter-fiscal-2026) (2025-11-19): Revenue reached $57 billion, up 62% year over year and 22% sequentially; diluted EPS was $1.30. This supports strong operating demand, not an automatic stock gain.

<a id="youtube-Lt0xLJJ6sfA-c006"></a>
### 006. Microsoft strong operations were obscured by concerns about capex and equity-method OpenAI losses.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

<a id="youtube-Lt0xLJJ6sfA-c007"></a>
### 007. Google and Microsoft should earn AI returns more easily than Meta because they already sell cloud services and Meta spends only on new products.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 6:45-7:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lt0xLJJ6sfA&t=405s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Current cloud revenue is relevant, but absence of a cloud segment does not imply no return from improving an existing advertising business. Meta current ad growth does not isolate AI returns either.

Assessment test: Estimate incremental returns within each existing and new business rather than compare labels.

- [Meta Q3 2025 results](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results/default.aspx) (2025-10-29): Revenue grew 26%, operating cash flow was $30 billion and quarterly free cash flow $10.62 billion. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities totaled $44.45 billion; capex, acquisitions, investments and shareholder distributions all affect cash balances.

<a id="youtube-Lt0xLJJ6sfA-c008"></a>

## Framework and tools

- Distinguish current cloud revenue from uncertain future monetization.
- Check funding capacity as capex rises.
- Differentiate a strong sector from a weak business model within it.
- Separate guidance, earnings quality and price reaction.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Hyperscaler capex
- Cash and marketable securities
- Operating cash flow and free cash flow
- Medical segment margins
- Payment volumes
- Same-store sales
